taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew treatment and native to Texas at state scale. Central Texas records in the current project review are dominated by horticultural or landscape use and are not promoted to native county evidence.
look_here_first: Think evergreen cherry: a small evergreen tree with glossy leathery alternate leaves, short axillary racemes of small white flowers, black drupes, and a bitter-almond odor when fresh twigs are scratched.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Latest manual review retained no qualifying wild project target-zone counties. Bexar and Travis references recovered were landscape/horticultural context; Williamson is outside the project target-county list.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification; preserve the HOLD.

best_field_traits: short axillary racemes of small white flowers
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Separate from P. serotina by evergreen glossy foliage and shorter axillary racemes; separate from P. mexicana by evergreen habit, glossy leaves, and cherry-like black fruit rather than larger plum-like drupes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Evergreen glossy foliage + short axillary racemes + black drupes is the strongest first-pass combination.
